around.headline: Bengaluru police launch manhunt after video of BMTC bus driver thrashing a harassment accused goes viral
around.summary: A woman alleged a man molested her on a moving bus; the driver stopped and confronted the accused, who fled before police arrived, and a sexual harassment case is now registered. If you witness harassment on a bus, alert the driver/conductor and call 100 or the women's helpline 1091 rather than trying to restrain the person yourself.
around.source: India Today / The Hindu / Deccan Herald

around.headline: Undercover cops ride BMTC buses for two weeks, nab pickpocketing duo
around.summary: Plainclothes officers posed as regular commuters on crowded routes before catching two serial pickpockets in the act. Keep bags zipped and valuables in front pockets on crowded buses — this is exactly the kind of route where they operate.

around.headline: Karnataka earmarks ₹450 crore to redevelop Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road from KR Pura to Silk Board
around.summary: The minister will meet stakeholders on the revamp plan as the CM separately floats a new tunnel-road project to ease congestion. If you commute along this ORR stretch, expect construction disruption before things improve.

around.headline: Bengaluru builder to demolish an 18-storey tower just 3 months after it got its occupancy certificate
around.summary: The tilted tower will be razed by Edifice, the firm behind the Noida Twin Towers demolition, after structural concerns emerged despite the fresh occupancy sign-off. A worthwhile reminder that an occupancy certificate alone isn't proof of structural safety — ask for a structural stability report before buying into a new tower.
around.source: The Hindu / The Times of India / Hindustan Times

around.headline: GBA towed just 54 of 5,133 abandoned vehicles flagged citywide
around.summary: The gap between flagged and actually-towed abandoned vehicles highlights weak follow-through on a civic drive meant to free up road and parking space. If an abandoned vehicle is blocking your street, report it directly to your ward office rather than assuming it's already logged.

around.headline: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns amid Gen Z-led 'Cockroach' protests over paper leaks
around.summary: The resignation is being called a major win for the youth-led protest movement that grew out of anger over recurring exam paper leaks. Worth watching if you or family are prepping for competitive exams — a leadership change often means a review of exam-security policy.

street_smart.title: You're on a crowded BMTC bus and see a man groping a woman a few seats away. She's shouting for help, and other passengers start moving in to grab and beat him before the next stop. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real case reported today: a BMTC bus driver stopped and thrashed a man accused of molesting a woman on board after she alleged harassment; the accused fled before police arrived, and a sexual harassment case is now registered while police hunt for him (India Today, The Hindu, Deccan Herald, News18).
street_smart.situation: The bus is packed, the accused is trying to slip out at the next stop, and voices are getting louder as some passengers move to physically stop him.

choices.text: Immediately alert the driver/conductor to hold the bus and doors at the stop, call 100 or the women's helpline 1091 with the bus route number and location, and film discreetly for evidence without joining any physical confrontation.
choices.feedback: Correct. This gets the bus physically held (so the accused can't simply walk off), gets police en route with exact identifying details, and preserves clean video evidence — all without turning bystanders into co-accused in an assault case.

choices.text: Join the other passengers in restraining and beating the man before police arrive.
choices.feedback: This is the trap: however justified the anger, group beatings on the spot routinely turn into assault or rioting charges against the bystanders themselves, and the chaos can let the actual accused later claim he was the one attacked. Physical restraint is for police to do — your job is to stop him from leaving and get them there fast.

choices.text: Film the incident on your phone but don't intervene or alert anyone, assuming another passenger will call the police.
choices.feedback: This is the bystander-effect trap — when everyone assumes 'someone else will call,' often no one does, and the accused simply exits at the next stop. Filming helps only if paired with actually alerting the driver and police.

choices.text: Shout at the man yourself to stop, but don't alert the driver or call the police.
choices.feedback: Verbal confrontation alone can make him bolt at the very next stop with no one having called it in — speaking up is good, but it only works if you also get the driver to hold the bus and get police on the way.

takeaways: On any harassment incident in public transport, alert the driver/conductor first — BMTC buses can be held at a stop, which is the single most effective way to stop someone from fleeing.
Call 100 (police) or 1091 (Karnataka women's helpline) with the bus route number and location, rather than relying on someone else to do it.
Avoid joining a group beating even against a clearly guilty person — it can get bystanders booked for assault/rioting and lets the real accused muddy the evidence.

quiz.why: It's named after André-Marie Ampère, a 19th-century French physicist considered one of the founders of electromagnetism.

quiz.q: In which year did India's Constitution come into effect?
quiz.why: India became a republic on 26 January 1950, which is why that date is celebrated as Republic Day, even though independence came on 15 August 1947.
